observation_summary: The DateTimeFormatter.parseInto method incorrectly overwrites the year of the provided instant with a default year (2000) during parsing, instead of using the year already present in the instant.
hypothesis: The DateTimeParserBucket was being initialized with a hardcoded or default year (iDefaultYear) instead of extracting the year from the provided instant, causing the parsed date to reset to the default year.
prediction: The fix will change the initialization of the DateTimeParserBucket to use the year from the instant instead of the iDefaultYear field.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows that the constructor call for DateTimeParserBucket was changed from using 'iDefaultYear' to 'chrono.year().get(instantLocal)', which directly confirms the hypothesis that the initialization value was incorrect.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of incorrect initialization. The code was using a fixed default year when it should have been using the year from the existing instant. This is not a missing check (Checking), nor a procedural logic error (Algorithm/Method), but a simple assignment of the wrong value during object initialization.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'parseInto now overwrites the given instant's year with 2000 (or whatever iDefaultYear is set to). The correct behavior would seem to be to use the given instant's year instead of iDefaultYear.'
The diff shows: - instantLocal, chrono, iLocale, iPivotYear, iDefaultYear); + instantLocal, chrono, iLocale, iPivotYear, chrono.year().get(instantLocal));

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a change in the procedural logic or computational steps, but rather a correction of the initial state (the year value) passed to the parser bucket.
